title: Tunable Statistics-Induced Caging in the Anyon-Hubbard Model
authors: Zenong Zhou, Chaorong Guo, Hongzheng Wu, Qianglin Hu, Xiaobing Luo
abstract: We study the quantum dynamics of two interacting anyons in the Anyon-Hubbard model on a four-site plaquette, a system that is exactly mappable to a Bose-Hubbard model. We reveal that static Aharonov-Bohm (AB) caging, induced by only specific statistical phases, emerges in the strongly interacting limit but breaks down under weak interparticle interactions. To address this, we demonstrate that statistical-factor-induced AB caging can be dynamically restored via Floquet engineering. This dynamical mechanism, governed by the synthetic Floquet flux and the anyonic statistical phase, extends the caging effect into the weakly interacting regime across the full spectrum of statistical phases. Furthermore, we show that the external drive enables the selective caging of anyons, providing an efficient approach for manipulating anyons and identifying statistical phases.
summary: The paper explores tunable statistics-induced caging in the Anyon-Hubbard Model by applying Floquet engineering. It shows that while intrinsic interactions can cause caging only under specific conditions (strong coupling), external high-frequency driving can dynamically restore this effect even when interactions are weak. This provides a powerful tool for selectively controlling anyonic behavior based on their underlying statistical phase.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum statistics can induce a controllable 'caging' effect for interacting anyons within the Anyon-Hubbard Model.
main_result: Dynamical control via Floquet engineering allows the restoration of this caging effect into the weakly interacting regime, enabling selective manipulation based on the statistical phase ($\kappa$).
method: The analysis employs mapping to a Bose-Hubbard model and utilizes high-frequency expansion methods (Floquet theory) combined with perturbation theory to derive effective Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The system is the Anyon-Hubbard Model on a four-site plaquette, which is exactly mapped to a Bose-Hubbard type Hamiltonian. The dynamics are governed by time-dependent Schrödinger equations solved via Floquet engineering techniques.
key_observables: Target site occupation $\langle \hat{n}_3(t) angle$ and its long-time average $\langle \hat{n}_3 angle$, which quantifies the degree of caging (suppression to zero).
important_parameters: Statistical phase ($\kappa$), hopping amplitude ($J$), interaction strength ($U$), and external drive parameters (amplitude $A$, frequency $\omega$, polarization angle $	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the anyonic system to a bosonic model and employing high-frequency approximations for the time evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the suppression of site occupation ($\langle \hat{n}_3 angle$) showing caging at specific parameter points, comparing results from effective Hamiltonians against full time-dependent simulations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing static caging in the strong interaction limit, then demonstrating its breakdown in weak coupling. The core contribution involves using Floquet engineering to dynamically restore this caging across all statistical regimes via an effective Hamiltonian approach.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses coherent control of quantum many-body states using time-periodic driving, a central theme in AMO physics and open quantum systems research.
